mainEntity.name: How much does air duct cleaning cost in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Air duct cleaning in Los Angeles typically costs $299–$599 for residential properties. The exact price depends on home size, vent count, and contamination level. Larger homes or those with significant mold/debris may cost more. Pure Air California provides free, no-obligation on-site estimates before any work begins.

mainEntity.name: Why do some companies charge only $49 or $99?

acceptedAnswer.text: Extremely cheap prices (under $150) are typically bait-and-switch tactics. These companies arrive, do a minimal surface cleaning of accessible vents, and then pressure sell you expensive add-ons ranging from $500–$2,000. The California Attorney General has warned consumers about this practice. Legitimate NADCA-certified cleaning (including full system access, negative pressure vacuum, and all components) costs $299+ for most homes.

mainEntity.name: What is included in your standard pricing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every Pure Air California service includes: inspection of the full duct system, negative air pressure setup to contain contaminants, cleaning of all supply and return air vents, main trunk line cleaning, HEPA-filtered vacuum extraction, and a final airflow verification test. We do not charge extra for register covers, basic tools, or travel within greater LA.

mainEntity.name: Do you offer free estimates?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We provide 100% free, no-obligation quotes by phone or online. For large homes or commercial properties, we recommend a brief on-site assessment so we can give you a firm price with no surprises. Call (213) 792-4145 or submit our online form.

mainEntity.name: Can I bundle dryer vent cleaning with air duct cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — bundling dryer vent cleaning with your air duct service saves you $50. Standalone dryer vent cleaning is $149–$249. Combined with an air duct cleaning appointment, it's only a $99 add-on.

mainEntity.name: Do you have financing or payment plans?

acceptedAnswer.text: We accept all major credit cards, cash, check, and Venmo. For commercial clients, we offer net-30 billing. Contact us if you need to discuss payment options for larger jobs — we are happy to work with you.

mainEntity.name: How much does commercial air duct cleaning cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Commercial air duct cleaning is priced per square footage and system complexity. Small commercial spaces (under 5,000 sq ft) typically start at $600. Larger office buildings, restaurants, or multi-unit properties receive custom quotes based on a site assessment. We offer after-hours scheduling to minimize business disruption.

mainEntity.name: How often should air ducts be cleaned?

acceptedAnswer.text: The National Air Duct Cleaners Association (NADCA) recommends cleaning air ducts every 3 to 5 years. In Los Angeles, wildfire smoke, smog, and year-round HVAC use mean every 2 to 3 years is common. Homes with pets, allergies, smokers, or recent renovations may benefit from more frequent cleaning.

mainEntity.name: How long does the air duct cleaning process take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical air duct cleaning for an average-sized home takes about 3 to 5 hours, depending on the size of your home, the number of vents, and the condition of your ductwork.

mainEntity.name: Will air duct cleaning reduce my energy bills?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Clean air ducts improve HVAC system efficiency, which can lower energy costs. When ducts are clogged with debris, your system works harder and uses more energy to heat and cool your home.

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if my air ducts need cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include visible dust or debris coming from vents, increased dust settling on surfaces, uneven airflow between rooms, musty odors when the system runs, and unexplained respiratory or allergy symptoms.

mainEntity.name: Is air duct cleaning worth the investment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Professional air duct cleaning improves indoor air quality, reduces allergens, increases HVAC efficiency, extends equipment life, and eliminates odors. Pure Air California is NADCA certified and provides free, no-obligation estimates.

mainEntity.name: How much does air duct cleaning cost in Los Angeles?

acceptedAnswer.text: Air duct cleaning in Los Angeles typically costs between $299–$599 for a standard residential property. The exact price depends on the number of vents, system size, and condition. Pure Air California provides free, no-obligation estimates — call (213) 792-4145 or use our online quote form.

mainEntity.name: How often should I have my air ducts cleaned in LA?

acceptedAnswer.text: The EPA and NADCA recommend professional air duct cleaning every 3–5 years. However, in Los Angeles — with its higher smog levels, wildfire smoke seasons, and year-round HVAC use — many homeowners clean every 2–3 years, especially those with pets, allergies, or recent renovations.

mainEntity.name: Does air duct cleaning make a real difference in LA air quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. Los Angeles air quality is already a challenge outdoors; your indoor HVAC system can actually make it worse if ducts are packed with dust, mold spores, or allergens. After cleaning, most customers notice reduced allergy symptoms, less dust settling on surfaces, and better airflow within 24 hours.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Pure Air California is fully NADCA-certified, California state-licensed, bonded, and insured. We are also A+ accredited with the Better Business Bureau. Every technician passes background checks and ongoing NADCA training.

Continue What your score actually means This calculator weighs the factors that most reliably predict how quickly a home's ductwork accumulates dust, allergens and moisture: the age of the property, whether pets live there, how long it has been since the system was last serviced, and where in Los Angeles County the home sits. None of those are guesses — they are the same things a technician asks about before quoting a job. Low risk Your system is likely in reasonable condition. A standard inspection every three to five years is usually enough, alongside regular filter changes. Moderate risk Enough factors are stacking up that accumulation is likely measurable. An inspection is worthwhile, particularly if anyone in the home has allergies or asthma. High risk Several compounding factors are present. A professional inspection is the sensible next step, and it is free — you will see photographs of your own ductwork either way. Why these factors matter Property age Older homes frequently still run their original ductwork. Systems built decades ago were not designed around modern filtration expectations, and in Los Angeles a great deal of the housing stock predates those standards entirely. Pre-war properties may also have sealed or undocumented access points, which is why inspection comes before cleaning. Pets in the home Dander is light enough to stay airborne and fine enough to pass through standard filtration, so it settles inside the duct run rather than being captured. Homes with multiple animals accumulate noticeably faster than homes without. Time since last service This is the single strongest predictor. Accumulation is cumulative and does not self-correct, so a system that has never been cleaned holds everything it has ever circulated. If you do not know when it was last done, assume it has not been. Where you live in LA County Location changes the load. Coastal properties contend with salt air and marine layer humidity; San Fernando Valley homes run their systems far longer through the summer; foothill and canyon properties take on wildfire ash and brush dust. Two identical houses in different parts of the county will not accumulate at the same rate. Common questions Is this a substitute for an inspection? No. It is a prioritisation tool. Only a physical inspection shows the actual condition of your ductwork, which is why we photograph it and show you. How often should air ducts be cleaned? For most Los Angeles homes, every three to five years is a reasonable interval. Pets, allergies, recent construction, wildfire exposure or a system that has never been cleaned all shorten it. Does duct cleaning help with allergies? It removes accumulated dust, dander and pollen from the system that circulates air through your home, which reduces what gets recirculated. It is one part of indoor air quality rather than a cure on its own. Get a Free Quote Explore Services How Clean Air Ducts Improve Your Health Your home's air ducts are the pathways through which heated and cooled air travels. When these ducts become filled with dust, allergens, pet dander, and other contaminants, these particles are circulated throughout your home every time your HVAC system runs. According to the EPA, indoor air can be 2-5 times more polluted than outdoor air. Since the average American spends about 90% of their time indoors, the quality of the air you breathe at home has a significant impact on your health and wellbeing. Relief for Allergy Sufferers For the estimated 50 million Americans who suffer from allergies, clean air ducts can provide significant relief by reducing exposure to common triggers: Pollen Reduction: Clean air ducts help prevent the circulation of seasonal pollens that can trigger hay fever and other allergic reactions. Pet Dander Control: Professional cleaning removes accumulated pet dander from your ductwork, reducing this common allergen throughout your home. Dust Mite Allergen Removal: Dust mites and their waste products are a leading cause of allergic reactions. Air duct cleaning helps remove these microscopic allergens. Mold Spore Elimination: Damp air ducts can harbor mold growth. Professional cleaning removes existing mold and helps prevent future infestations. Common Allergy Symptoms Reduced by Clean Air Ducts: Sneezing and runny nose Itchy, watery eyes Congestion and sinus pressure Scratchy throat Skin irritation and rashes Headaches Many of our clients with allergies report significant improvement in their symptoms within days of having their air ducts professionally cleaned. Asthma Management and Respiratory Health For the 25 million Americans with asthma, including 7 million children, clean air ducts can play a crucial role in managing symptoms and reducing attacks. Asthma triggers commonly found in dirty air ducts include: Dust and Particulate Matter Microscopic dust particles can irritate the bronchial tubes and trigger asthma attacks. Professional air duct cleaning removes these particles from your ventilation system. Mold and Mildew Mold spores are potent asthma triggers. Air duct cleaning eliminates mold growth within your HVAC system, preventing these spores from being distributed throughout your home. Chemical Irritants Cleaning products, VOCs, and other chemical residues can accumulate in air ducts. Removing these irritants helps reduce respiratory inflammation and asthma symptoms. Bacterial and Viral Pathogens Viruses and bacteria that can trigger respiratory infections may circulate through dirty air ducts. Regular cleaning helps reduce these potential pathogens in your home. Research on Indoor Air Quality and Asthma According to the American Lung Association, improving indoor air quality is one of the most effective strategies for managing asthma. Studies have shown that reducing airborne triggers through measures like air duct cleaning can: Decrease the frequency and severity of asthma attacks Reduce the need for rescue medications Improve lung function and breathing capacity Decrease emergency room visits and hospitalizations Enhance overall quality of life for asthma sufferers Additional Health Benefits of Air Duct Cleaning Reduced Odors Eliminate persistent musty or stale odors by removing the source—contaminants in your air ducts. Improved Energy Better sleep and reduced exposure to allergens and toxins can lead to increased energy levels. Enhanced Sleep Clean air can lead to better quality sleep by reducing nighttime allergy symptoms and breathing issues. schema.description: Our professional 5-step air duct cleaning process ensures your home's air quality is restored.

step.name: Initial Inspection
step.text: Our technicians start by thoroughly examining your ductwork, vents, and HVAC system to assess the level of contamination and identify any potential issues that need addressing.

step.name: System Preparation
step.text: We carefully prepare your home by covering furniture and flooring near vents. We then create negative pressure in the ductwork using professional-grade equipment to ensure that dust and debris are contained during the cleaning process.

step.name: Thorough Cleaning
step.text: Using specialized tools, including rotary brushes and high-powered vacuum systems, we dislodge and remove accumulated dust, debris, and contaminants from your entire duct system, including supply and return ducts, registers, and diffusers.

step.name: Sanitizing Treatment
step.text: Upon request, we can apply an EPA-approved sanitizing treatment to your cleaned ductwork to eliminate remaining bacteria, fungi, and mold spores, and help prevent future microbial growth.

step.name: Final Inspection & Cleanup
step.text: After cleaning, our technicians perform a final inspection to ensure all ducts are thoroughly cleaned. We then replace all access panels, restore system components, and clean the work area.

mainEntity.name: How often should I have my air ducts cleaned?

acceptedAnswer.text: The National Air Duct Cleaners Association (NADCA) recommends having your air ducts cleaned every 3-5 years. However, homes with pets, residents with allergies, recent renovations, or visible mold growth may benefit from more frequent cleaning (every 1-2 years).

mainEntity.name: How long does the cleaning process take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical residential air duct cleaning for an average-sized home takes approximately 3-5 hours. Larger homes or systems with significant contamination may take longer. We provide a firm time estimate during our initial assessment.

mainEntity.name: Will air duct cleaning help my allergies?

acceptedAnswer.text: Absolutely. Our process removes accumulated dust, pollen, pet dander, and other allergens. Many of our customers report a noticeable reduction in allergy symptoms and respiratory irritation within 24 hours of our service.

mainEntity.name: Is your process noisy or messy?

acceptedAnswer.text: We use high-powered, truck-mounted or portable HEPA vacuums that are designed to be relatively quiet. We use drop cloths and specialized containment strategies to ensure your home remains spotless throughout and after our visit.

mainEntity.name: Why should I choose Pure Air California over cheaper alternatives?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many 'coupon' companies only do a surface cleaning. We are NADCA certified, fully insured, and use industrial-grade equipment to clean the entire system, including the furnace, blower motor, and coils—not just the vents.

acceptedAnswer.text: A restricted vent forces the dryer to run longer to shift the same moisture, so it burns more gas per load. Clearing the restriction shortens cycles. The size of the saving depends on how restricted the system had become, which is why we document the before condition.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, and they are among the most commonly neglected systems we see, because no individual resident treats the vent as their responsibility. We coordinate with property management on scheduling and resident notice.

mainEntity.name: How often does a commercial kitchen exhaust system need cleaning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Frequency depends on cooking volume and fuel type. High-volume and solid-fuel kitchens typically need quarterly or monthly service, while lower-volume operations are often on a semi-annual or annual schedule. Your local fire authority and insurer may set a specific interval.

mainEntity.name: Is grease buildup in the exhaust really a fire risk?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Grease deposits inside hoods, ducts and fans are combustible, and a flare-up on the cooking line can ignite them and carry fire through the duct run into the roof structure. Removing the fuel is the point of the service.

mainEntity.name: Will cleaning interrupt service?

acceptedAnswer.text: We schedule overnight or during closed hours so the kitchen is ready for the next service period. Surfaces are protected and the line is left clean.

mainEntity.name: Do you clean the dining room air ducts too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Kitchen exhaust and the dining room HVAC are separate systems. Cleaning the dining-side ductwork addresses cooking odors and airborne grease that migrate into the seating area and settle on surfaces.

mainEntity.name: What makes industrial duct cleaning different from commercial work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Industrial systems handle process dust, welding fume, oil mist and other contaminants that ordinary office HVAC never sees. The ductwork is larger, often runs at height, and requires equipment and access planning suited to a plant environment.

mainEntity.name: Does combustible dust accumulation in ductwork need to be addressed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Accumulated combustible dust inside ducts and on overhead surfaces is a recognized deflagration hazard, and housekeeping of those surfaces is a standard part of an industrial fire-prevention program.

mainEntity.name: Can cleaning happen without shutting down production?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually. We work around planned maintenance windows, shift changes and scheduled shutdowns, and can section the work so only part of the system is offline at a time.

mainEntity.name: Do you provide documentation for compliance records?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We supply written service reports with before-and-after documentation for each area, which plants retain for OSHA recordkeeping and insurance inspections.

At Pure Air California, we receive many questions about our services. This comprehensive guide answers the most common questions about professional air duct cleaning. What is Air Duct Cleaning? Air duct cleaning is the process of removing dust, debris, allergens, mold, and other contaminants from your home's HVAC system. This includes the supply and return air ducts, registers, grilles, diffusers, heat exchangers, cooling coils, condensate drain pans, and air handling unit components. Professional cleaning uses specialized tools and techniques to dislodge contaminants and vacuum them out of your system, preventing them from recirculating throughout your home. What Are the Benefits of Air Duct Cleaning? The major benefits of professional air duct cleaning include: Improved Indoor Air Quality: Removes allergens, dust, and pollutants that would otherwise circulate through your home Enhanced Energy Efficiency: Clean ducts allow your HVAC system to operate more efficiently, potentially reducing energy costs Extended HVAC Lifespan: Reduces strain on your system, potentially extending its operational life Reduced Allergens: Particularly beneficial for allergy and asthma sufferers Elimination of Odors: Removes musty smells that can develop from mold, mildew, or other contaminants Cleaner Living Environment: Less dust circulating means less dust settling on your furniture and surfaces How Often Should Air Ducts Be Cleaned? The National Air Duct Cleaners Association (NADCA) recommends cleaning your air ducts every 3 to 5 years. However, certain circumstances may warrant more frequent cleaning: Homes with pets or high shed animals Residents with allergies, asthma, or respiratory conditions Recent home renovations or construction Moving into a new home (especially if the previous owners had pets) Visible mold growth inside ducts or on HVAC components Pest or rodent infestation in ducts Water damage or flooding affecting HVAC system What Does the Air Duct Cleaning Process Involve? Our professional air duct cleaning process typically includes: Inspection: We begin with a thorough inspection of your HVAC system using specialized cameras Protection: We protect your home by laying down floor coverings and ensuring proper containment Negative Pressure: We create negative pressure in the system using commercial-grade vacuum equipment Agitation: We use specialized tools to dislodge debris from duct surfaces Cleaning: We clean all registers, grilles, and accessible components Sanitizing: Optional EPA-approved sanitizing treatments to eliminate bacteria and fungi Final Inspection: We conduct a post-cleaning inspection to ensure all contaminants have been removed How Much Does Air Duct Cleaning Cost? The cost of air duct cleaning varies based on several factors: Size of your home or building Number of HVAC systems Number of vents and returns System accessibility Level of contamination Additional services (sanitizing, deodorizing, etc.) For a typical single-family home in Los Angeles, air duct cleaning generally ranges from $350 to $700. We provide detailed, transparent pricing with free on-site estimates before beginning any work. How Long Does Air Duct Cleaning Take? For an average-sized home, professional air duct cleaning typically takes 3 to 5 hours. Larger homes or systems with significant contamination may require 6 to 8 hours. Our technicians work efficiently while ensuring thorough cleaning. Can Air Duct Cleaning Improve Health Issues? Many clients report health improvements after professional air duct cleaning, particularly those with allergies, asthma, or respiratory sensitivities. Clean air ducts can reduce the circulation of allergens like pollen, pet dander, dust mites, mold spores, and bacteria. By addressing these contaminants, air duct cleaning can contribute to a healthier indoor environment and potentially reduce symptoms for sensitive individuals. Ready to Take Action? Secure Your Slot Pure Air California Home Home About Health Benefits Services Industries Locations Blog 24/7 Premium Support (213) 792-4145 Get a Quote Safety Dryer Vent Safety Guide Fire Safety Expert February 28, 2026 3 min read Home Blog Dryer Vent Safety Guide Back to Blog Most homeowners don't think about their dryer vents until there's a problem. However, neglected dryer vents represent one of the most significant fire hazards in American homes. According to the U.S. Fire Administration, approximately 2,900 home dryer fires are reported each year, causing an estimated 5 deaths, 100 injuries, and $35 million in property loss. Why Dryer Vents Become Dangerous Every time you dry a load of laundry, lint particles separate from your clothes. While your dryer's lint trap catches much of this material, significant amounts still pass through into the venting system. Over time, this lint accumulates along the walls of your dryer vent, creating three serious problems: 1. Fire Hazard Lint is highly flammable. When it accumulates in your dryer vent, it creates perfect conditions for a fire. The high heat from your dryer can cause lint to ignite, and once it does, the fire can quickly spread through the vent to your walls and throughout your home. 2. Reduced Efficiency & Higher Energy Costs When lint blocks your dryer vent, the hot, moist air from your dryer cannot escape efficiently. This forces your dryer to work harder and run longer to dry your clothes, consuming more energy and increasing your utility bills. Many homeowners report savings of $25-35 per month after a thorough dryer vent cleaning. 3. Premature Appliance Failure The strain placed on your dryer from a clogged vent shortens its operational lifespan. Components like heating elements, thermostats, and motors wear out faster when your dryer runs longer and hotter than necessary. Warning Signs Your Dryer Vent Needs Cleaning Watch for these telltale indicators that it's time for dryer vent maintenance: Clothes taking longer than one cycle to dry (more than 30-40 minutes for a typical load) Dryer exterior feels excessively hot during operation Burning smell when the dryer is running Excessive lint accumulating around the lint filter or dryer opening No visible lint on the exterior vent hood when the dryer is running Bathroom-like humidity in your laundry room during dryer operation Visible debris around your outdoor dryer vent opening How Often Should Dryer Vents Be Cleaned? The National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) recommends that dryer vents be inspected and cleaned at least once per year. However, several factors may warrant more frequent cleaning: High-volume households doing many loads of laundry weekly Homes with pets that shed significant hair and dander Long or complex dryer vent runs with multiple bends or turns Older dryer models with less efficient lint trapping systems Drying heavy items like towels, bedding, or rugs frequently The Professional Dryer Vent Cleaning Process While some homeowners attempt DIY cleaning with brushes or vacuums, professional dryer vent cleaning offers much more thorough results and peace of mind. Here's what our professional process includes: Comprehensive Inspection: We examine your entire dryer vent system, from the connection at the dryer to the exterior vent, identifying any damage, disconnections, or code violations. Professional Equipment: We use specialized rotary brushes and high-powered vacuum systems designed specifically for dryer vents. Complete Cleaning: Our process removes 100% of lint buildup, not just the accessible portions near the connections. Airflow Verification: After cleaning, we test the system to ensure proper airflow has been restored. Yet many businesses overlook this essential aspect of workplace management until problems arise. The Business Case for Better Indoor Air Quality Research consistently demonstrates that indoor air quality has a measurable impact on business performance. Consider these compelling statistics: Enhanced Productivity: Studies by Harvard University and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory found that improved ventilation and reduced indoor pollutants can increase worker productivity by 8-11%. Reduced Absenteeism: The EPA estimates that poor IAQ contributes to approximately $60 billion in annual productivity losses due to employee sick days. Energy Cost Savings: Clean HVAC systems operate more efficiently, potentially reducing energy consumption by 5-15%. Extended Equipment Life: Regular maintenance of ventilation systems extends the useful life of costly HVAC equipment. Improved Customer Experience: For retail, hospitality, and service businesses, air quality directly impacts customer comfort and perception. Common Indoor Air Quality Issues in Commercial Buildings Commercial properties face unique air quality challenges due to their size, occupancy patterns, and mechanical systems. The most common issues include: 1. Ventilation Inadequacies Many commercial buildings—particularly older structures—suffer from insufficient fresh air exchange. Modern energy conservation measures sometimes exacerbate this problem by tightly sealing buildings without adequately addressing ventilation needs. 2. Duct Contamination Over time, commercial air ducts accumulate dust, allergens, mold spores, and other contaminants. When HVAC systems operate, these particles circulate throughout the building. Regular commercial air duct cleaning is essential for removing these pollutants. 3. Moisture and Mold Issues Commercial HVAC systems generate significant condensation, which can lead to moisture accumulation and mold growth if not properly managed. This is particularly problematic in humid climates or buildings with water damage history. Signs Your Commercial Building Has Air Quality Problems Watch for these warning indicators that your facility may need air quality attention: Pattern of employee complaints about headaches, fatigue, or respiratory irritation Visible dust around air vents or on surfaces shortly after cleaning Uneven temperatures throughout your facility Musty or stale odors , particularly when HVAC systems first activate Visible moisture or water stains on ceiling tiles or walls Excessive dust buildup in server rooms or on electronic equipment Higher than expected utility bills despite normal usage patterns Comprehensive Solutions for Commercial Air Quality Improvement Enhancing commercial indoor air quality requires a multi-faceted approach: 1. Professional Air Duct Cleaning Commercial air duct cleaning removes accumulated contaminants from your HVAC distribution system, preventing them from circulating throughout your facility. Our commercial cleaning process uses negative air pressure technology and specialized equipment to thoroughly clean even the largest commercial systems. 2. HVAC System Upgrades and Maintenance Regular HVAC maintenance ensures proper operation and prevents issues like microbial growth and system inefficiency. Consider installing higher-efficiency filtration systems, regular filter replacement schedules, and cleaning of coils, drain pans, and other HVAC components. 3. Advanced Filtration Solutions Commercial electrostatic filter systems offer significant advantages over traditional filters. These systems capture particles as small as 0.3 microns, are washable and reusable, maintain airflow while providing superior filtration, and offer lower lifetime costs. The Cost-Benefit Analysis When evaluating the investment in commercial air quality improvements, consider both direct and indirect returns. Most businesses find that the combined benefits far outweigh the investment costs of comprehensive air quality improvements. Every business is unique, and air quality solutions should be tailored to your specific needs, building characteristics, and budget. Contact Pure Air California today to discuss how we can help your business achieve optimal indoor air quality. Ready to Take Action? According to the EPA, indoor air can be 2-5 times more polluted than outdoor air, and the average American spends approximately 90% of their time indoors. This makes the quality of your indoor air a critical factor in maintaining good health. Understanding Indoor Air Pollution Before examining the benefits of clean air ducts, it's important to understand what builds up inside your ventilation system over time. The typical home's air ducts can accumulate: Dust and dust mites - Including dead skin cells, fabric fibers, and microscopic organisms Pet dander - Tiny particles of skin shed by cats, dogs, and other animals Pollen - From trees, grasses, and plants that enters through windows or on clothing Mold spores - Particularly in humid environments or systems with moisture issues Bacteria and viruses - Which can survive and multiply in ductwork Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) - From cleaning products, paints, and furnishings Key Health Benefits of Professional Air Duct Cleaning 1. Reduction of Allergy and Asthma Symptoms For the 50 million Americans who suffer from allergies, clean air ducts can provide significant relief. When professional cleaning removes allergens from your ventilation system, these triggers aren't continuously recirculated throughout your home. The benefits include: Decreased frequency and severity of allergy attacks Reduced nasal congestion, sneezing, and itchy eyes Fewer asthma triggers, potentially reducing the need for medication Improved sleep quality due to easier nighttime breathing 2. Respiratory Health Protection Even individuals without diagnosed allergies or asthma benefit from cleaner indoor air. Clean air ducts contribute to respiratory health by: Reducing irritation of mucous membranes in the nose, throat, and lungs Decreasing coughing and throat irritation Lowering the risk of bronchial infections Supporting healthy lung function for all ages 3. Mold Prevention and Elimination Moisture in air ducts creates an ideal environment for mold growth. Once established, mold releases spores into your home's air, potentially causing allergic reactions, sinus infections, headaches, and in severe cases, lung inflammation. 4. Improved Sleep Quality The quality of air you breathe during sleep directly impacts how well you rest. Clean air ducts contribute to better sleep by reducing nighttime congestion and breathing difficulties, minimizing coughing that can wake you, and creating a more comfortable sleeping environment. Special Health Considerations Certain populations may experience greater benefits from clean air ducts: Children: Their developing respiratory systems are more vulnerable to air quality issues Elderly individuals: May have naturally declining immune function and higher sensitivity to pollutants People with compromised immune systems: Require special attention to reduce exposure to potential pathogens Pregnant women: May experience increased sensitivity to odors and irritants How Often Should Air Ducts Be Cleaned for Health Benefits? To maintain the health benefits of clean air ducts, follow these general guidelines: Every 3-5 years for homes without special concerns Every 2-3 years for homes with pets, smokers, or residents with allergies/asthma Every 1-2 years for homes with elderly or immunocompromised residents After major renovations that generate significant dust Upon moving into a new home (unless documentation of recent cleaning exists) If you or your family members suffer from allergies, respiratory conditions, or simply want to create the healthiest possible home environment, professional air duct cleaning is a valuable investment in your wellbeing. While many focus on visible dust and dander, one often overlooked contributor to indoor allergens is your air duct system. In this article, we'll explore how professional air duct cleaning can significantly reduce allergy symptoms and create a healthier home environment. The Allergy-Air Duct Connection Your home's air ducts serve as the respiratory system of your living space, circulating air throughout every room. Unfortunately, they can also become collection points for common allergens: Dust mites and their waste products Pet dander Pollen from trees, grasses, and flowers Mold spores and bacteria Insect remains When your HVAC system runs, these allergens can be distributed throughout your home, triggering symptoms in sensitive individuals. For those with asthma or severe allergies, this continuous exposure can lead to chronic discomfort and health issues. Common Allergy Symptoms Related to Poor Indoor Air Quality Many allergy sufferers experience worse symptoms indoors than outdoors, which often points to air quality issues within the home. Common symptoms include: Sneezing and runny nose Itchy, watery eyes Coughing and throat irritation Skin rashes or hives Headaches Fatigue Difficulty breathing or wheezing If you notice these symptoms worsening when you're at home or when your heating or cooling system is running, contaminated air ducts could be contributing to your discomfort. How Professional Air Duct Cleaning Helps Professional air duct cleaning removes accumulated allergens from your entire HVAC system. Here's how this process benefits allergy sufferers: 1. Removal of Allergen Reservoirs Over time, your air ducts can collect pounds of dust and allergens. Professional cleaning removes these reservoirs, preventing them from being circulated throughout your home. This is especially important in older homes or properties that haven't had duct cleaning services in many years. 2. Elimination of Mold and Bacteria Moisture in air ducts can lead to mold growth, which releases spores that trigger allergic reactions and respiratory issues. Professional cleaning not only removes existing mold but can also include antimicrobial treatments to prevent future growth. 3. Reduced Dust Circulation Clean air ducts mean less dust being circulated and settling on surfaces throughout your home. This reduces the overall allergen load and means less frequent dusting and cleaning are needed to maintain good air quality. 4. Improved HVAC Efficiency Clean ducts allow your HVAC system to work more efficiently, providing better air filtration and temperature control. This creates a more comfortable environment and can extend the life of your air filters, further improving air quality. Real Results for Allergy Sufferers Many of our clients report significant improvement in their allergy symptoms after professional air duct cleaning. For example, Jennifer from Beverly Hills shared: "After years of struggling with indoor allergies, I was amazed at how much better I felt just days after Pure Air California cleaned our air ducts. The constant sneezing and itchy eyes I experienced at home have virtually disappeared." Research supports these experiences. Studies have shown that proper HVAC system maintenance, including regular air duct cleaning, can significantly reduce airborne allergens in indoor environments. Additional Steps for Allergy Relief While air duct cleaning is a powerful tool for improving indoor air quality, combining it with other strategies can provide even greater relief: Use high-efficiency air filters (MERV 11 or higher) and change them regularly Consider installing a whole-home air purification system Maintain indoor humidity between 30-50% to discourage dust mite and mold growth Vacuum frequently using a HEPA-filtered vacuum cleaner Remove shoes at the door to prevent tracking in outdoor allergens Wash bedding weekly in hot water When to Schedule Air Duct Cleaning for Allergies For allergy sufferers, we recommend scheduling air duct cleaning: Before allergy season begins (typically early spring in Los Angeles) After home renovations or construction projects When moving into a new home Every 2-3 years for maintenance (more frequently for severe allergy sufferers) By prioritizing clean air ducts, you're making a significant investment in your health and comfort. Over time, these ducts can accumulate dust, debris, allergens, and even mold, compromising your indoor air quality and potentially causing health issues. But how do you know when it's time to schedule a professional air duct cleaning? 1. Visible Dust Around Vents One of the most obvious signs that your air ducts need cleaning is visible dust accumulation around your air vents. If you notice dust building up shortly after cleaning, it could indicate that your ductwork is releasing dust into your home. This is especially concerning because what you see around the vents is just a fraction of what may be inside your entire duct system. Professional cleaning can remove this built-up debris and prevent it from circulating throughout your home. 2. Increased Allergy Symptoms If you or your family members are experiencing increased allergy symptoms while indoors, your air ducts could be the culprit. Dirty air ducts can harbor allergens like pollen, pet dander, and dust mites, which are then circulated throughout your home whenever your HVAC system runs. Common symptoms include: Sneezing Coughing Itchy eyes Congestion Respiratory issues 3. Mold or Mildew Odors If you notice a musty or mildew-like smell when your air conditioning or heating system turns on, this could indicate mold growth within your ductwork. Moisture can accumulate in air ducts, creating an ideal environment for mold to thrive. Mold in air ducts is particularly concerning because your HVAC system can spread mold spores throughout your entire home, potentially causing health issues, especially for those with respiratory conditions or compromised immune systems. 4. Reduced Airflow or Efficiency If you've noticed decreased airflow from your vents or that some rooms in your home aren't heating or cooling as effectively as they used to, clogged air ducts might be the issue. Significant dust and debris buildup can restrict airflow, forcing your HVAC system to work harder to maintain your desired temperature. This not only leads to discomfort but can also increase your energy bills and shorten the lifespan of your HVAC equipment due to the additional strain. 5. Recent Renovation or Construction Home renovation or construction projects generate significant amounts of dust and debris that can infiltrate your duct system. If you've recently completed a remodeling project, it's advisable to have your air ducts inspected and cleaned to remove any construction particles that may have accumulated. Even with precautions like sealing vents during construction, fine dust particles can still find their way into your ductwork. When to Schedule Professional Air Duct Cleaning The National Air Duct Cleaners Association (NADCA) recommends having your air ducts cleaned every 3 to 5 years. However, you might need more frequent cleaning if: You have pets that shed fur and dander Someone in your home suffers from allergies or asthma You've had a mold problem or water damage You live in an area with high pollution or construction You notice any of the signs mentioned above Professional air duct cleaning by Pure Air California involves a thorough cleaning of all components of your forced air system, including supply and return air ducts, registers, grilles, diffusers, heat exchangers, heating and cooling coils, condensate drain pans, and the air handling unit housing. Benefits of Regular Air Duct Cleaning Investing in regular air duct cleaning offers numerous benefits: Improved indoor air quality Reduced allergens and irritants Elimination of musty odors Enhanced HVAC efficiency Lower energy bills Extended HVAC system lifespan By addressing these signs early and scheduling professional air duct cleaning, you can ensure your home maintains optimal air quality and your HVAC system operates at peak efficiency. Industrial air duct cleaning helps facilities meet: OSHA General Duty Clause: Employers must provide workplaces free from recognized hazards OSHA 29 CFR 1910.94: Ventilation requirements for abrasive blasting, grinding, and spray finishing NFPA 652: Standard on combustible dust fundamentals Cal/OSHA Title 8: California-specific industrial safety orders SCAQMD Rules: South Coast Air Quality Management District emissions requirements Non-compliance can result in fines exceeding $100,000 and potential facility shutdowns. Combustible Dust: A Hidden Danger Combustible dust explosions have caused numerous fatalities and millions in property damage. Industries at risk include: Food processing (sugar, flour, grain, spices) Woodworking and lumber mills Metal fabrication (aluminum, magnesium, titanium) Pharmaceutical manufacturing Chemical processing Textile and paper production Regular industrial duct cleaning removes accumulated dust before it reaches dangerous concentrations. The Restaurant Ventilation Challenge Commercial kitchens generate far more airborne contaminants than any other indoor environment: Grease vapor: Cooking fat becomes airborne and coats duct surfaces Smoke particles: From grilling, roasting, and high-heat cooking Food particles: Fine debris from food preparation and cooking Humidity: Steam from cooking creates moisture that combines with grease Odors: Cooking smells that can permeate dining areas if not properly exhausted Fire Hazard: LA's Hidden Restaurant Risk Grease accumulation in kitchen exhaust systems is a leading cause of restaurant fires. According to NFPA: Cooking equipment is involved in 61% of restaurant fires Failure to clean is a factor in 22% of restaurant fires Grease buildup in ducts and hoods allows fires to spread rapidly to other areas A single restaurant fire averages $23,000 in damage—not counting business interruption The Los Angeles Fire Department requires regular cleaning of commercial kitchen exhaust systems, with frequency based on cooking volume and type. Health Department Requirements The Los Angeles County Department of Public Health inspects restaurants for proper ventilation maintenance: Hood and duct cleanliness: Visible grease accumulation is a violation Proper airflow: Exhaust systems must effectively remove smoke and steam Filter maintenance: Grease filters must be clean and in good condition Documentation: Records of professional cleaning may be requested A failed health inspection can result in closure, fines, and devastating negative publicity on platforms like Yelp. Cleaning Frequency Requirements NFPA 96 establishes minimum cleaning frequencies based on cooking operations: Monthly: High-volume cooking (24-hour operations, charbroiling, wok cooking) Quarterly: Moderate-volume cooking (most full-service restaurants) Semi-Annually: Low-volume cooking (churches, day camps, seasonal operations) Annually: Systems serving ovens only (no frying or grilling) What Professional Restaurant Duct Cleaning Includes Our restaurant ventilation cleaning service covers: Exhaust Hoods: Complete degreasing of hood interior, including plenums and light fixtures Ductwork: Cleaning entire duct run from hood to rooftop fan Exhaust Fans: Blade, housing, and motor cleaning Grease Filters: Cleaning or replacement as needed Access Panels: All panels opened and cleaned, properly resealed after service Rooftop Equipment: Fan and discharge area cleaning Beyond Kitchen Exhaust: Restaurant HVAC Don't forget your restaurant's supply air ducts, which also need attention: Dining room comfort affects customer satisfaction and reviews Grease particles can contaminate supply air systems HVAC cleanliness impacts employee health Clean supply ducts reduce odors in dining areas Insurance and Liability Your insurance company may require documentation of regular hood and duct cleaning. This intensive use creates significant lint accumulation that, without proper maintenance, becomes a serious fire hazard and efficiency problem. The Laundromat Fire Risk Commercial dryers in laundromats face far greater lint accumulation than residential units: A typical laundromat dryer runs 8-10 hours daily vs. 1-2 hours for home dryers Higher capacity drums process more fabric, generating more lint per cycle Customer use of incorrect heat settings can accelerate lint production Public facilities can't control what items customers dry (lint-heavy towels, pet bedding, etc.) The U.S. Fire Administration reports that failure to clean dryer vents is the leading cause of dryer fires. For laundromats, this risk is multiplied by usage volume. Warning Signs Your Laundromat Needs Vent Cleaning Watch for these indicators of lint accumulation: Extended drying times: Clothes requiring multiple cycles to dry Excessive heat: Dryer exteriors hot to the touch Customer complaints: About damp clothes after full cycles Visible lint: Around dryer connections or vent terminations Burning smell: Lint beginning to overheat High energy bills: Dryers working harder due to restricted airflow Shutoff interruptions: Thermal safety switches cutting power Commercial Dryer Vent Cleaning Frequency Unlike residential dryers that need annual cleaning, laundromat vents require more frequent service: High-volume locations: Every 3 months Moderate-volume locations: Every 6 months Low-volume locations: Annually at minimum Additionally, lint traps should be cleaned by staff after every load ideally, but at minimum daily. Efficiency and Cost Savings Clogged dryer vents directly impact your bottom line: Energy costs: Restricted airflow forces dryers to run longer, using 30% or more extra energy Customer satisfaction: Longer drying times lead to complaints and lost business Equipment wear: Overworked dryers fail sooner—commercial dryers cost $3,000-$8,000 to replace Repair costs: Overheating damages heating elements, thermostats, and motors For a 20-dryer laundromat, proper vent maintenance can save $300-500 monthly in energy costs alone. This guide cuts through the confusion and tells you exactly what professional air duct cleaning should cost in LA in 2026, what's included, and how to avoid the scams that the California Attorney General has warned consumers about. What is the Average Cost of Air Duct Cleaning in Los Angeles? For a typical Los Angeles home, professional NADCA-certified air duct cleaning costs $299 to $599 . Here's how that breaks down by home size: Studio / 1-bedroom (under 800 sq ft): $299–$349 2–3 bedroom home (800–1,800 sq ft): $349–$449 — most common for LA homeowners 4+ bedroom / large home (1,800–3,500 sq ft): $449–$599 Dryer vent cleaning (add-on): $99 bundled / $149–$249 standalone EPA sanitizing treatment: $75–$150 add-on Commercial air duct cleaning starts at $599 for small offices and is priced by square footage and system complexity for larger properties. What's Included in That Price? A legitimate air duct cleaning service in Los Angeles should include all of the following at no extra charge: Inspection of the entire duct system (supply and return lines) Negative pressure setup using HEPA-filtered vacuum equipment Cleaning of all supply and return air vents and registers Main trunk line cleaning Blower motor and air handler inspection Post-cleaning airflow verification test Written estimate before work begins — price confirmed, no surprises Why Do Some Companies Advertise $49 or $99 in LA? These prices are almost always bait-and-switch tactics. The California Attorney General's office has received thousands of complaints about this exact practice. Here's how the scam typically works: You book a $49 or $99 cleaning, attracted by the low price Technicians arrive and do a minimal surface wipe of visible vents They then fabricate problems — "Your ducts are severely contaminated," "We found dangerous mold" — with no documentation They pressure you to approve $500–$2,000+ in additional services on the spot If you refuse, they leave, having done almost nothing despite taking payment Red flags: No NADCA certification. No physical LA address. No Google reviews with real names. Refuses to give a written quote before starting. High-pressure sales tactics on arrival. What Factors Affect the Price in LA? The final cost of air duct cleaning in Los Angeles depends on: Number of vents: More vents = more labor. Average LA home has 12–20 supply and return vents. Duct accessibility: Ducts in slabs, tight crawl spaces, or behind drywall take more time. Contamination level: Heavy mold, rodent droppings, or construction dust require additional steps. Number of HVAC systems: Many LA homes over 2,500 sq ft have two separate systems. Add-on services: Sanitizing, coil cleaning, electrostatic filter installation. Is Air Duct Cleaning Worth the Cost in LA? For most Los Angeles homeowners, yes — especially if you haven't had it done in 3+ years, have pets or allergies, or recently experienced wildfire smoke. (2026 Guide) Michael Rodriguez, NADCA Certified April 1, 2026 4 min read Home Blog Should You Clean Your Air Ducts After a Wildfire in Los Angeles? (2026 Guide) Back to Blog With wildfire seasons becoming longer and more intense across Southern California, millions of Los Angeles residents face a critical question after fires like the Palisades, Eaton, or Woolsey fires: should I have my air ducts cleaned after wildfire smoke exposure? The short answer is almost always yes — and here's why. How Wildfire Smoke Gets Inside Your Duct System Even when you keep doors and windows closed during a wildfire event, smoke infiltrates your home through multiple entry points: HVAC fresh air intakes: Most HVAC systems draw fresh air from outside. During a wildfire, this intake pulls smoke directly into your duct system. Unsealed gaps: Older LA homes, especially those built before 1980, often have gaps around light fixtures, electrical outlets, and ductwork connections. Return air vents: Any smoke that enters your living space gets drawn back into the duct system through return vents. Running your HVAC during a fire: Many residents run AC to stay comfortable when it's hot — this actively pulls smoke in and deposits it throughout the ductwork. What's Actually in Wildfire Smoke That Stays in Your Ducts? Wildfire smoke is far more complex and dangerous than ordinary household dust. It contains: PM2.5 ultra-fine particles: These penetrate deep into lungs and are linked to cardiovascular and respiratory disease. Once in your ducts, they recirculate for months. Toxic combustion byproducts: When homes, cars, and structures burn, they release benzene, formaldehyde, heavy metals, and asbestos (from older structures). Ash particles: Visible ash settles throughout ductwork and continues releasing chemicals as it breaks down. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs): Known carcinogens from incomplete combustion that adhere to duct surfaces. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs): From burned plastics, electronics, and materials — some remain active for months. Signs Your Ducts Were Affected by Wildfire Smoke Smoky smell when your HVAC runs — even weeks after the fire Visible soot or ash around vent registers Gray or brown discoloration on supply vents Family members experiencing headaches, coughing, or eye irritation indoors Air filters turning dark gray within days (normal is 30–90 days) Musty or chemical smell mixed with smoke odor When Should You Have Ducts Cleaned After a Wildfire? The timing matters. Here's our recommendation for LA homeowners: Immediately (during/just after fire): Change your HVAC filter to the highest MERV rating your system can handle (MERV 13+). Set your AC to recirculate inside air only, not fresh air intake, until smoke clears. Within 2–4 weeks after fire: Schedule professional air duct cleaning. This is the optimal window — smoke has settled and contaminated the system, but hasn't yet deeply penetrated porous duct materials. Homes within 5 miles of burn area: Strongly recommended regardless of visible symptoms. Ultra-fine particles don't always leave visible residue. Homes outside the immediate area: If your area had AQI above 150 for 3+ consecutive days, duct cleaning is recommended. Does Homeowner's Insurance Cover Post-Wildfire Duct Cleaning? This is one of the most important questions we get after a fire event. In many cases, yes — especially if your home suffered smoke damage. Here's what to do: Document the smoke damage with photos and air quality readings (AQI data from airnow.gov during the fire is admissible) File a claim for smoke and ash infiltration Request that air duct cleaning be part of your remediation plan Get a professional inspection report — Pure Air California provides before-and-after documentation that insurers accept California insurance law requires coverage for smoke damage. Do not auto-remediate before filing a claim — document everything first. But by then, months or years of contamination have already been circulated through your home. This guide covers the 7 most reliable warning signs that your LA home needs professional air duct cleaning — including several that are unique to Southern California's environment. 1. Visible Dust Around Vents Shortly After Cleaning If you clean your home's surfaces thoroughly and notice dust re-accumulating around air vents within a few days, your duct system is almost certainly the source. The visible dust you see settling on furniture and shelves is just a fraction of what's inside your ducts, being continuously blown into your living spaces every time the HVAC runs. LA-specific context: Homes near the 405, 101, or 110 freeways receive constant traffic-related particulate infiltration. Even with sealed windows, ultra-fine particles enter through HVAC fresh air intakes and accumulate in ductwork faster than in areas with cleaner outdoor air. 2. Worsening Allergy or Asthma Symptoms Indoors If you or family members feel worse at home than outside — sneezing, congestion, coughing, or itchy eyes — your indoor air quality may be the cause. Los Angeles already struggles with one of the worst outdoor air quality records in the US. When your duct system becomes a reservoir for those pollutants plus pet dander, dust mites, mold spores, and pollen from year-round blooming, your indoor air can actually be far more polluted than the air outside. Signs this is duct-related vs. general allergy: symptoms worsen specifically when the AC or heater runs; symptoms improve when you are away from home for several days; other family members with no outdoor allergies develop symptoms indoors. 3. Musty, Stale, or Smoky Smell When HVAC Starts A musty odor when your system first kicks on usually indicates mold or mildew growth inside the ductwork or on the evaporator coil. This is particularly common in LA's coastal neighborhoods (Santa Monica, Venice, Malibu, Marina del Rey) where marine layer humidity provides ideal mold-growing conditions inside HVAC systems. A smoky or chemical smell that persists months after a wildfire in your area means smoke particles have bonded to your duct surfaces and are being re-vaporized every time the system heats up. This requires immediate professional attention and possible insurance claim filing. 4. Rooms Feel Stuffy or Have Inconsistent Temperatures Significant debris buildup inside ductwork restricts airflow. When airflow is restricted, certain rooms get less conditioned air — they feel stuffy in summer and cold in winter even while other rooms are comfortable. If your HVAC thermostat is set correctly but some rooms never reach the right temperature, dirty ducts are a likely culprit. In older LA homes from the 1950s–1980s (common in neighborhoods like Silver Lake, Highland Park, Mid-City, and the Valley), original ductwork may also have gaps, deteriorating insulation, or collapsed sections that compound this problem. 5. Your Energy Bills Have Increased Without Explanation When ducts are partially blocked by debris or leaking conditioned air into unconditioned spaces (attics, crawl spaces), your HVAC system works harder and longer to maintain your set temperature. This directly increases your energy consumption and monthly utility bills. If your LADWP or SoCalGas bill has crept up 15–25% without a change in usage patterns, duct inefficiency may be the cause. Studies show clean, properly sealed air ducts can improve HVAC efficiency by 25–40%. For the average LA homeowner paying $150–$250/month in cooling costs during summer, that's meaningful monthly savings that can offset the cost of professional cleaning in just a few months. 6. You've Recently Had Home Renovation or Construction Construction and renovation work is the single fastest way to contaminate an HVAC duct system. Drywall dust, insulation fibers, wood particles, and concrete dust easily find their way into supply and return vents. Even with vents taped off during construction, debris still infiltrates through gaps over the course of a weeks-long project. LA's ongoing residential renovation boom — ADU construction, kitchen remodels, earthquake retrofitting — means a large percentage of homes are in or recently completed renovation. If you've had work done in the past 2 years and haven't cleaned your ducts since, scheduling a cleaning is strongly recommended. 7. It's Been More Than 3 Years (or You've Never Had It Done) The National Air Duct Cleaners Association (NADCA) recommends cleaning every 3–5 years for most homes. In Los Angeles — where HVAC systems run nearly year-round due to climate, where wildfire smoke is a seasonal reality, and where smog infiltration is a constant — many NADCA-certified professionals recommend every 2–3 years for homes near high-traffic corridors or in fire-prone areas. If you've moved into a home and don't know when the ducts were last cleaned, schedule a professional inspection. Homes change hands in LA with surprising frequency, and it's common to find duct systems that haven't been touched in 10+ years. An Honest Answer Pure Air California Team September 4, 2026 5 min read Home Blog Is Air Duct Cleaning Worth It? An Honest Answer Back to Blog It is a fair question, and the honest answer is that it depends on your system and your household — not on whether someone can sell you the job. Air duct cleaning is genuinely worthwhile in some situations and close to pointless in others. Anyone who tells you it is always necessary is selling; anyone who tells you it never matters has not looked inside enough ductwork. Here is how to tell which situation you are in. What the research actually says The US Environmental Protection Agency's position is more measured than most marketing suggests. The EPA does not recommend duct cleaning as a routine measure for every home on a fixed schedule. It does recommend it when there is visible mould growth inside the ducts or on other components of the system, when ducts are infested with vermin, or when ducts are clogged with substantial deposits of dust and debris that are actually being released into the home. The National Air Duct Cleaners Association, the industry's certifying body, recommends inspection every three to five years, with cleaning performed when the inspection shows it is needed. Note the distinction: inspect on a schedule, clean on evidence. That is the standard we work to, and it is why we inspect before quoting rather than quoting over the phone. When it is clearly worth doing There is visible mould in the system. This is the least ambiguous case. If growth is established on duct surfaces, the coil or the drain pan, the system is distributing spores every time it runs. Cleaning and sanitising addresses the source. After a fire, or after nearby wildfire smoke. Smoke and fine ash are drawn into the intake and settle inside the ductwork, where they keep recirculating long after outdoor air has cleared. This is the case Los Angeles homeowners most often skip, because the house looks untouched. It is also the one where cleaning makes the most measurable difference. After renovation or construction. Drywall dust is fine enough to pass through standard filtration and abrasive enough to matter once it reaches the blower. If work was done with the system running, or with vents unsealed, the ducts collected it. Vermin or an obvious infestation. Droppings and nesting material in ductwork are a genuine health issue, not an aesthetic one. You have just moved in and nobody knows the history. Homes change hands often, and a system that has not been inspected in fifteen years is common. An inspection settles it either way. Someone in the house has asthma or significant allergies and symptoms are worse indoors. Clean ducts are not a cure, and it would be dishonest to promise otherwise. But if the system is genuinely loaded, removing that load removes one input. When it is probably not worth it This is the part most companies leave out. Your ducts were cleaned two years ago and nothing has changed. No renovation, no fire, no water damage, no new pets, no symptoms. Cleaning again on a calendar rather than on evidence is spending money for very little. Your real problem is airflow, not contamination. Weak airflow from the registers is at least as often a failing capacitor, low refrigerant, a badly sized or clogged filter, or a duct that has come apart in the crawl space. Those need an HVAC technician, not a duct cleaner. We will tell you when that is what we find, and we do not charge to tell you. You want it done to fix an odour with an obvious other source. A dead animal under the house, a dry P-trap, or a failing drain pan will not be solved by cleaning the ducts, and paying to find that out is avoidable. The house is brand new and nothing has been done to it. Occasionally worth checking for construction debris. Rarely worth a full clean. The dryer vent question is different If you are weighing air duct cleaning, weigh dryer vent cleaning separately, because the case is stronger and it is not primarily about air quality. A blocked dryer vent is a fire risk, and it is a well-documented one. Lint accumulates in the duct run, the dryer works harder and hotter to push air through it, and the combination of restricted airflow and heat is exactly the condition that starts fires. The practical signal is simple: if clothes now take two cycles to dry when they used to take one, the vent is restricted. That is worth acting on regardless of what you decide about the air ducts. What a fair price looks like in Los Angeles Residential air duct cleaning in Los Angeles generally runs $299 to $599 depending on system size, the number of vents and the condition of the ductwork. Dryer vent cleaning generally runs $149 to $249. Larger or multi-zone properties cost more because there is genuinely more work. If you are quoted $79 for a whole-house duct cleaning, that price does not cover the labour to do the job properly. What follows on the day is almost always a much larger number. We wrote a separate guide on how to recognise that pattern before a technician is in your home . How to decide Get an inspection before you get a quote, and make sure the inspection is free and carries no obligation. Ask to be shown what is actually in the system rather than shown a stock photograph. A company confident in its findings will have no difficulty with either request. Pure Air California has been NADCA certified and working across Los Angeles County for over forty years. If an inspection shows your ducts do not need cleaning, we will tell you so. Secure Your Slot Pure Air California Home Home About Health Benefits Services Industries Locations Blog 24/7 Premium Support (213) 792-4145 Get a Quote FAQ How to Avoid Air Duct Cleaning Scams in Los Angeles Pure Air California Team September 4, 2026 5 min read Home Blog How to Avoid Air Duct Cleaning Scams in Los Angeles Back to Blog Air duct cleaning has a bait-and-switch problem, and Los Angeles has it worse than most markets. The pattern is consistent enough that both the Federal Trade Commission and the National Air Duct Cleaners Association have published warnings about it. Knowing the shape of it is usually enough to avoid it. This is written by a company that competes with those operators, so read it with that in mind. Everything below is checkable independently, and we would rather you verified it than took our word. The $79 whole-house special This is the core of it. An advertised price of $69, $79 or $99 for a whole-house duct cleaning is not a discount, because it is not a price anyone can perform the work for. A genuine residential duct cleaning takes a two-person crew several hours with truck-mounted or substantial portable equipment. The arithmetic does not reach $79 at any volume. What the number buys is an appointment. Once a technician is inside, the job is re-scoped: extra vents charged individually, a mandatory sanitising treatment, a "severe contamination" surcharge, a separate charge for the main trunk line. Bills of $700 to $2,000 from a $79 advertisement are routine. A fair Los Angeles price is $299 to $599 for residential air duct cleaning and $149 to $249 for a dryer vent. A quote far below that range is not a better deal on the same work. The mould finding that appears on arrival A common escalation is the discovery of dangerous mould shortly after arrival, accompanied by urgency and a substantially larger quote. Sometimes there really is mould — coastal and marine-layer areas of Los Angeles genuinely do support growth inside ductwork. What separates a real finding from a manufactured one is evidence. Ask to be shown the growth in your own system, on a camera feed or in a photograph taken inside your ducts on that visit. Ask what the substance is. Not all dark deposit is mould, and confirming it properly requires testing rather than a glance. If the answer is a stock image, a laminated brochure or pressure to decide immediately, stop and get a second opinion. Real findings survive a second opinion. Certification you can actually verify NADCA certification is the industry standard, and it is verifiable — NADCA maintains a public directory of member companies at nadca.com. Anyone can print a logo on a van. Look the company up. Check the California contractor licence too, through the Contractors State License Board at cslb.ca.gov. Ask whether the company carries liability insurance, and ask for the certificate rather than an assurance. These are ordinary questions and a legitimate company answers them without friction. Warning signs worth taking seriously Unsolicited calls or door-knocking. Established duct cleaning companies do not generally cold-call. This is a strong signal on its own. A firm price before anyone has seen the system. Duct cleaning cost depends on system size, vent count and condition. A confident number over the phone means either the number will change or the work will be minimal. Pressure to decide immediately. Ductwork is not an emergency. Any offer that expires today is a sales technique, not a schedule constraint. Cash only, or a large deposit up front. Legitimate companies take normal payment methods and generally bill on completion. Claims about health benefits that sound like medicine. Clean ducts can reduce circulating dust and allergens. They do not cure asthma, and a company promising that is telling you something about itself. No verifiable address or a company name that changes. Search the phone number. Operations that rebrand frequently do so for a reason. Four questions worth asking Before booking anyone, including us: Are you NADCA certified, and what name are you listed under so I can check? What is included in the quoted price, and what would add to it? Will you show me the inside of my ducts before and after? Are you licensed and insured, and can I see the certificate? Four straightforward questions. A company that answers all four plainly is very unlikely to be the problem. If it has already happened If you have been overcharged or pressured, you can file a complaint with the California Attorney General's office, the Contractors State License Board where a licensed contractor is involved, and the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov. Complaints matter more than people assume: enforcement follows patterns, and patterns are built from individual reports. How we work Pure Air California is NADCA certified, licensed and insured, and has operated in Los Angeles County for over forty years. We inspect before quoting, we show you what is in your system, and if the inspection shows the ducts do not need cleaning we will say so. Our pricing is published on our pricing page rather than discovered on the day. If you are weighing whether the work is needed at all, our guide on whether air duct cleaning is worth it covers the cases where the honest answer is no.
